subject: Immediate: ClearBuy inference backlog causing failures — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina@clearbuy.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sustained latency & 5xx spike (ClearBuy account)

Sean —

Sorry to ping so early. We started seeing a sustained latency increase and a wave of 5xx responses across our inference endpoints this morning (around 07:40 PDT). Impact: downstream order validation times jumped from ~120ms to >1.2s for ~30% of requests and our retry fanout caused additional 5xx errors.

We pulled logs and attached a small sample (clearbuy-error-log-2025-04-15.txt). Key observations from our side:
- The errors are primarily 5xx (internal server) returned intermittently, not client errors.
- The latency increase tracks with peak token throughput around 07:30–08:00.
- Our traffic profile didn’t change — same QPS and same prompt sizes.

We rely on Reserved Capacity (monthly commitment) for predictable throughput. We suspect we hit some saturation point in the dedicated GPU pool and requests were being queued/failed. Can you confirm if there was any capacity event on Redwood this morning?

This is blocking our late-morning batch window — raising as P1. Please advise ASAP.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Head of Platform Ops, ClearBuy

Attachment: clearbuy-error-log-2025-04-15.txt (text, 78KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Torres <lina@clearbuy.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 08:53:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production: sustained latency & 5xx spike (ClearBuy account) — initial triage

Sean / Marissa / Lina — initial findings from short triage run:

What we see (quick summary):
- Evidence of dedicated GPU pool saturation on the cluster serving ClearBuy's reserved instances. CUDA utilization for the relevant workers hit sustained >96% during the window Lina reported.
- Request queue length on the serving fleet increased sharply; KV cache pressure caused more cache warms and token compute per request rose modestly (~5–8%).
- There were drops in worker availability as some tasks were OOM-killed when bursts overlapped with background maintenance jobs (kernel selection/quantization warm-ups).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low friction):
1) Short-term: enforce a soft QPS cap for ClearBuy via tenant throttling (reduces tail latency by limiting queue depth). Requires ops approval for temporary restriction of reserved throughput.
2) Reroute a safe percentage of ClearBuy traffic to a compatible hosted model variant (lower-cost, slightly lower throughput) — preserves capacity while we clear backlog. We should confirm acceptance with customer; this is a graceful fall-back.
3) Emergency burst: request allocation of additional burst capacity from capacity pool (requires leadership approval).
4) Engineering fix: postpone non-essential background maintenance/compaction on the affected nodes for the next 2 hours.

I'll start with a blocking test (apply a 15% soft throttle) and monitor metrics if you approve. Also attaching a short diagnostics brief (redwood-diagnostics-brief-CLB.pdf) with graphs.

Why this is different than a routing bug: reserved capacity should have prevented this headroom drop under typical traffic — the combination of unexpected background jobs + KV cache warms pushed the system past the failover thresholds. We need to treat this as both capacity and runtime stability.

Proposed customer communication (to send within 45m): a short note acknowledging the impact, stating immediate mitigations (throttle + reroute + burst request), and committing to a full RCA within 48h.

Irene Choi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-diagnostics-brief-CLB.pdf (8 slides)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production: sustained latency & 5xx spike (ClearBuy account) — exec coordination

Thank you for the rapid triage. I reviewed the diagnostics — this looks like a capacity saturation + runtime fragility event and warrants exec visibility. My asks:

1) Customer comms: Sean/Marissa please send a concise note to Lina by 16:15 PDT confirming the mitigations we're applying (soft throttle now, reroute 20% traffic, requesting emergency burst capacity) and provide an ETA for when we expect normal latencies to return (target: 90 minutes).

2) Ops authorization: Irene — proceed with the 15% throttle immediately and request the burst allocation. If the burst comes back delayed beyond 30 minutes, escalate to me and I will sign-off on temporary credit/compensation if needed.

3) Executive brief: Marissa — prep a one-page exec brief (bullet points + key metrics: pre/post latency, 5xx rate, queue depth) and post to the HubSpot incident record and Drive link in the related_links. I want this in my inbox within 60 minutes.

4) Post-mortem: schedule a cross-functional RCA with infra, runtime, and CS within 48 hours. Include a remediation plan for background maintenance gating during peak windows and improvements to reserved capacity enforcement.

We should be explicit with the customer about root cause hypotheses rather than promising a specific fix. Good initial work — keep me posted.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
